**Finding submitted: deviation (Section 13.5, Ownership).**

**Issue.** Section 13.5 otherwise tracks our preferred position — Developments (including interface coding created solely by Corio) are owned by Corio, Commerce One assigns any claim it might have, and Commerce One's pre-existing materials and Software ownership (§2.8) are preserved. The problem is the embedded carve-out: if Commerce One supports a Development "on an ongoing basis," Commerce One retains **all** ownership rights in IP that Corio created and paid for. That is a walk-away item under the rule (assignment of Customer IP to Vendor), and it conflates a support arrangement with a title transfer.

**Redline (validated, ok:true).**
- p0115: delete ", unless such Developments are supported on an ongoing basis by Commerce One in which case Commerce One will retain all ownership rights, including" and close the sentence at "shall be owned by Corio."
- p0116: delete the now-orphaned fragment "intellectual property rights in the Developments." so the paragraph opens cleanly at "To the extent that Commerce One would otherwise have a claim of ownership..."

**Left as-is deliberately.** The final sentence of p0116 (ownership of enhancements/derivatives *of the Software itself* to be negotiated before work starts) is a reasonable existing bargain, since those are derivatives of Commerce One's licensed Software. There is no Customer Data concept in this hosting/reseller agreement, so no data-ownership sentence was added. Fallback offered in the comment: a support-purposes licence to Commerce One instead of ownership.
